title: Jeremy Pargo buries ten threes for 48 as Grindavik seize Icelandic crown on the road
description: Jeremy Pargo (188-PG-1986, college: Gonzaga) produced one of the most extraordinary individual performances in Icelandic basketball history on Sunday, erupting for 48 points on 10-of-16 from three-point range to power Grindavik to a 109-102 road victory over Tindastoll in Game 4 and clinch the Bonus Deildin Karla championship 3-1 before 1,653 fans. The American guard was simply unguardable. Shooting 16-of-23 from the field overall (69%), he added eight rebounds and eight assists a whisker from a triple-double for a staggering 53 efficiency in 38 minutes. When Tindastoll rallied in the fourth quarter to make a game of it with a 30-25 final period, it was Jeremy Pargo who had the answers every single time.
imageCaption: Jeremy Pargo buries ten threes for 48 as Grindavik seize Icelandic crown on the road (Photo: IG)

title: Stjarnan edge Tindastoll to conquer Subway League title
description: Tindastoll - Stjarnan 77-82 Stjarnan clinched Subway League title. They nipped Tindastoll in the decisive fifth game of the championship series. The guests trailed by 5 points after three quarters before their 18-8 charge, which allowed them to win the game. American-Puerto Rican guard Jase Febres (196-1999, college: Texas) stepped up with a double-double by scoring 12 points, 16 rebounds and 5 assists for the winners and the former international guard Hilmar Henningsson (195-2000) chipped in 20 points and 4 assists. American point guard Dedrick Basile (178-1994, college: CSUB) responded with 14 points, 9 rebounds and 7 assists and the former international point guard Sigtryggur Bjornsson (180-1993, college: St.Mary's) scored 18 points and 6 rebounds. Five Tindastoll players scored in double figures.
imageCaption: Stjarnan edge Tindastoll to conquer Subway League title (Photo: karfan.is)

title: Valur topple Grindavik to earn Dominos League title
description: Valur - Grindavik 80-73 Valur clinched Dominos League title. They held off Grindavik in the Finals decider. Valur outrebounded Grindavik 51-36 including 17 on the offensive glass. Irish-British forward Taiwo Badmus (200-1993, college: UVA Wise) orchestrated the victory with a double-double by scoring 31 points and 14 rebounds. The international swingman Kristinn Palsson (198-1997, college: Marist) contributed with 17 points and 8 rebounds for the winners. Hungarian-American swingman DeAndre Kane (195-1989, college: Iowa St.) answered with 17 points, 9 rebounds and 4 assists and American point guard Dedrick Basile (178-1994, college: CSUB) added 16 points and 7 assists in the effort for Grindavik. Four Grindavik players scored in double figures.
imageCaption: Keflavik roll past Tindastoll to claim Cup title (Photo: Keflavik)

title: Tindastoll are 22/23 Subway League champions
description: Valur - Tindastoll 81-82 Tindastoll are 22/23 champions. They nipped Valur in the exciting fifth game of the championship series to conquer the trophy. The guests trailed by 13 points after first quarter, but they rallied back winning next two quarters and won the game by 1 point. The best player for the winners was American Keyshawn Woods (192-1996, college: Ohio St.) who scored 33 points (!!!) and 5 rebounds. The former international guard Petur Birgisson (187-1996) chipped in 9 points, 11 rebounds, 8 assists and 4 steals. The former international guard Kari Jonsson (192-1997, college: Drexel) produced 19 points, 7 rebounds and 6 assists and the former international forward Kristofer Acox (198-1993, college: Furman) added 16 points and 7 rebounds respectively for the hosts. Five Valur players scored in double figures.
imageCaption: Tindastoll are 22/23 Subway League champions (Photo: visir.is)

title: Valur celebrate Dominos League title
description: Valur - Tindastoll 73-60 Valur claimed Domins League title. They held off Tindastoll in the decisive fifth game of the championship series to conquer the trophy. The hosts were tied at the half but managed to speed up in last two quarters eventually winning the game. Valur forced 19 Tindastoll turnovers and outrebounded them 52-40 including 16 on the offensive glass. The former international forward Kristofer Acox (200-1993, college: Furman) stepped up with a double-double by scoring 13 points and 19 rebounds for the winners and international forward Hjalmar Stefansson (203-1996) chipped in 24 points and 5 rebounds (on 11-of-14 shooting from the field). Irish-British forward Taiwo Badmus (201-1993, college: UVA Wise) responded with 17 points and 7 rebounds and American guard Javon Bess (198-1996, college: St.Louis) produced a double-double by scoring 13 points and 10 rebounds.
imageCaption: Valur celebrate Dominos League title (Photo: visir.is)

title: Thor Thorl celebrate Dominos League title
description: Thor Thorl - Keflavik 81-66 Thor Thorl earned Dominos League title. They beat Keflavik in the fourth game of the championship series to lift the trophy. The hosts trailed by 6 points after first quarter, but they stormed back to get the 3-point lead at the halftime and eventually won the game 81-66. Thor Thorl looked well-organized offensively handing out 22 assists. Worth to mention a great performance of Lithuanian center Adomas Drungilas (205-90) who helped to win the game recording a double-double by scoring 24 points and 11 rebounds. American point guard Larry Thomas (185-93, college: BSC, agency: SDJ Sports) contributed with a triple-double by scoring 11 points, 12 rebounds and 11 assists for the winners. Thomas is a former Eurobasket Summer League player, which is considered top international summer league in the market. Four Thor Thorl players scored in double figures.…
imageCaption: Thor Thorl celebrate Dominos League title (Photo: karfan.is)
